_comment: The install matrix, declaratively. matrix.sh reads this through cells.mjs; docs/testing-installs.md says how to add a cell. Container images other than the product's own are named ONLY here (they are pulled at run time; nothing is added to npm or NuGet).

cells.name: docker-direct
cells.description: The release image on a fresh named volume, port bound to 127.0.0.1, plain http, forceHttps OFF: the baseline every other cell is read against.

data-root.description: data.db is owned by root inside the image user's folder (what a restore run as root leaves behind)

cells.name: docker-forcehttps-http
cells.description: server.forceHttps is ON but the instance is reached over plain http. The session cookie is Secure, so a browser drops it: sign-in answers 200 and no session is kept (the sign-in button stays on "Signing in..."). The journey must report it as session not kept, and the Connection check must say why.

expect: c=session not kept: forceHttps is on and the page is plain http, so the Secure session cookie is dropped by a browser

cells.name: docker-nginx-good
cells.description: nginx:alpine in front on a Docker network: gzip on for JSON, Host / X-Forwarded-For / X-Forwarded-Proto set, TLS with a self-signed certificate made at run time, forceHttps ON, server.knownProxies set to the Docker network's own range. The documented setup, end to end; nginx weakens the ETag when it gzips (issue 63).

logAbsent.pattern: Forwarding headers .* not listed in server\.knownProxies
logAbsent.why: a trusted proxy must not draw the untrusted-proxy warning

nginx-no-proto.description: nginx stops sending X-Forwarded-Proto while server.forceHttps is off (the common nginx setup that relies on that header to tell the server the visit was https)

nginx-untrusted-proxy.description: server.knownProxies is not set, so the server ignores the proxy's forwarded headers and every visitor shares one address for the sign-in throttle

cells.name: docker-nginx-noproto
cells.description: The same nginx, but WITHOUT X-Forwarded-Proto and with server.knownProxies unset: the server does not trust the proxy, so every visitor shares one address for the sign-in throttle. With forceHttps on, the Secure cookie still works over https, so the journey passes; what must be caught is the lockout hazard: the Connection check warns about the proxy and the log carries the untrusted-proxy line.

logExpect.pattern: Forwarding headers .* not listed in server\.knownProxies
logExpect.why: the lockout warning: forwarded headers arrived from a peer the server does not trust

cells.name: docker-caddy
cells.description: caddy:2 in front with encode gzip and automatic internal TLS (Caddy's own local CA), forceHttps ON, knownProxies set to the Docker network range. (Observed: Caddy's encode honours the server's Cache-Control: no-transform, so it leaves the responses and the ETag alone.)

logAbsent.pattern: Forwarding headers .* not listed in server\.knownProxies
logAbsent.why: a trusted proxy must not draw the untrusted-proxy warning

cells.name: docker-cloudflare-like
cells.description: A small Node proxy (cfproxy.mjs) standing in for Cloudflare: TLS, gzips JSON, REWRITES the strong ETag to W/"..." (issue 63), adds CF-Connecting-IP and X-Forwarded-Proto: https, strips nothing else. The journey must pass and report the ETag as weakened.

expectNote.why: the ETag must arrive weakened in this cell, or the cell is not reproducing issue 63

proxy-strip-versions.description: the proxy removes the ETag AND X-Document-Version, so a save has nothing to quote in If-Match

cells.name: docker-cloudflare-noetag
cells.description: Variant of docker-cloudflare-like where the proxy removes the ETag entirely. The journey must still pass, saving with X-Document-Version, and report the ETag as missing.

expectNote.why: the ETag must be missing in this cell

cells.name: archive-macos
cells.description: The real osx-arm64 release archive, unpacked on this Mac and run with a bare PATH (env -i) on a fresh data folder, direct on 127.0.0.1. Nothing but the archive is installed.

cells.name: archive-linux-clean
cells.description: The Linux release archive for Docker's architecture, run inside a bare ubuntu:24.04 container (no .NET, no Node installed) as a non-root user, data folder on a bind mount owned by that user, direct.

cells.name: upgrade-newest
cells.description: The newest fixture under tests/upgrade-fixtures (a data folder an earlier build wrote through its own API) opened by the CURRENT image: every document, user, token, version and setting must come through (scripts/upgrade-fixture/verify.mjs), and then the whole journey runs as the fixture's administrator.

cells.name: upgrade-oldest
cells.description: The same, from the OLDEST fixture, so the migrations actually run (4 of 8 applied when it was made). The pre-migration copy is made and the data survives.

manual.name: windows-archive
manual.description: The win-x64 or win-arm64 release archive on Windows (a Windows VM). Not run by matrix.sh: the VM uses about 13 GB, so a person starts it. The journey itself runs from this Mac against the VM's address (--vm), so the same steps are judged.
manual.why: needs the Windows VM (13 GB); start it deliberately, then run the commands below
commands: # 1. Start the VM (UTM). On the VM, unpack draughtsman-<version>-win-arm64.zip (or win-x64) and run, in PowerShell:
#    (the setup code is printed to the console; as a service it is in C:\dmx-data\setup-code.txt and `draughtsman first-run-code`)
# 2. From this Mac, copy the code in a file and run the journey against the VM's address (no --container: the verbs run on the VM):
node scripts/install-matrix/journey.mjs --base-url http://$(ssh windows-vm 'hostname -I' | awk '{print $1}'):5180 --setup-code-from file:./setup-code.txt

manual.name: dogfood-cloudflare
manual.description: A real server behind nginx and Cloudflare. The journey run against its https address is the acceptance test for the connection-layer fixes (weak ETag, session, proxy trust).
manual.why: needs the real server and a person's judgement of its result; it creates a throw-away administrator only on a fresh instance, so on a live one use --sign-in-as
commands: # On a FRESH instance (no users yet): the setup code comes from the server's log.
# (if the log is on another host: ssh root@<host> 'docker logs draughtsman-app 2>&1 | grep "setup code"' and put the code in a file, then --setup-code-from file:./code.txt)
# On an instance that already has an administrator: sign in as that person (the password is read from the environment, never from argv):
DMX_PASSWORD='<the administrator password>' node scripts/install-matrix/journey.mjs --base-url https://draughtsman-app.overpass.co.uk --sign-in-as you@example.com --password-env DMX_PASSWORD
